what_happened.line: The Board of Assessors voted to have Town Counsel review a draft deeds policy and homeowner letter and advise on any added legal language.
The board agreed not to pay the aerial-imagery (near map) invoice for now; it had been held unpaid during budget issues and the town manager transition.
Members discussed starting a multi-year review of neighborhood site indexes in-house, using money in the town manager's proposed budget rather than a large consultant.
The board discussed the Clause 41A/17 income and asset limits warrant article and asked for an estimate of its financial effect and its effect on overlay.
The board signed motor vehicle excise abatement paperwork, set the senior exemption design committee's first meeting for February 19, and entered executive session.

why_it_matters: Neighborhood site indexes feed how homes are grouped and valued for assessment, so an in-house review that runs several years could shift individual assessments, though the minutes state no outcome.
The Clause 41A/17 limits article would be a warrant vote for residents, and the board's request for an overlay estimate points to a possible effect on the tax rate; the minutes give no figure.
A three-year Vision inspection contract was signed by the interim town manager, though the assessors had wanted one year, which commits assessing funds beyond a single budget cycle.
watch_next: February 19, around 5:30 on Zoom: first meeting of the senior means-tested exemption design committee.
The Town Counsel response on the deeds policy letter and the Clause 41A/17 warrant article.
